last.verdict: EVgo cut its 2026 revenue and stall-build targets again, and the $2.00 takeover bid from majority owner LS Power now matters more than the quarter.

takeaways.label: Second guidance cut
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue outlook fell to $375-400M from $400-430M, new stalls to 1,075-1,275 from 1,350-1,625, and the EBITDA loss widened to $15-30M. Management blamed softer charging volumes and fewer, better sites.

takeaways.label: Core charging is growing
takeaways.text: Charging revenue rose 29% to $72M, but total revenue slipped 1% to $91.4M because partner-build (eXtend) revenue halved to $16M. Charging per stall fell 4% to 283 kWh a day.

takeaways.label: Buyout bid pending
takeaways.text: LS Power, with about 56% of the votes, offered $2.00 a share in cash on Nov. 2. A special committee is reviewing it, and management declined further comment.

takeaways.label: Losses and borrowing grow
takeaways.text: Net loss widened to $49.2M from $28.4M. Cash fell to $98.7M from $151M at year-end, and long-term debt rose to $312M from $204M. Management cited about $787M of liquidity.

history.verdict: Investors sold EVgo after the company cut its full-year outlook and cash burn rose.

reasons.label: Lower 2026 outlook
reasons.text: Revenue guidance cut to $400-430M from $410-470M; below analysts' roughly $433M.

reasons.label: Bigger expected losses
reasons.text: Full-year adjusted EBITDA now a $5-25M loss, versus a range reaching up to +$20M before.

reasons.label: Cash and slower ramp
reasons.text: Operating cash burn widened and new stalls ramped slower than hoped, despite Tesla deal.
